stateKeys.name: policy
stateKeys.type: enum: '' | 'hold' | 'continue' — what an escalated card does to the batch. Chosen once at START and immutable after: a run cannot change the rules it is being judged by halfway through.

stateKeys.name: pending
stateKeys.type: integer 0..3 — cards selected for this generation that have not yet settled

stateKeys.name: escalated
stateKeys.type: integer 0..2 — cards that reached needsHuman during this generation

dataFields.count: integer - how many specs this generation covers; chosen from the sekkei's new and changed nodes

dataFields.policy: string - 'hold' (an escalation stops the batch) or 'continue' (the batch runs on and reports what escalated). The user's call, recorded in the run.

specialRules.name: select-only-while-drafting
specialRules.note: The set of specs is chosen before the generation starts and never after: a batch whose membership can change mid-run has no meaningful 'finished'.

specialRules.name: start-needs-a-selection
specialRules.note: START applies only in drafting, and only with at least one spec selected.

specialRules.name: policy-is-chosen-once
specialRules.note: The escalation policy is recorded at START and never changes. Both values are legal — which one is right is the user's call, and the checker proves the machine behaves correctly under either.

specialRules.name: card-outcomes-only-while-running
specialRules.note: A card outcome arriving outside running — late, duplicated, or after the batch settled — is absorbed as an observable no-op.

specialRules.name: hold-stops-the-batch
specialRules.note: Under policy 'hold', a card reaching needsHuman moves the generation to held: no further card is started until a person resumes. Under 'continue' the batch runs on and the escalation is carried into the terminal state instead. This is the one behavioural difference between the two policies.

specialRules.name: resume-only-from-held
specialRules.note: RESUME_GENERATION is the human's decision to carry on after a hold. It exists nowhere else, and it never clears the escalation count — the batch remembers what it stepped over.

specialRules.name: settled-generations-name-their-outcome
specialRules.note: A generation finishes as 'done' only when nothing escalated. If any card reached needsHuman, it finishes as 'doneWithEscalations' — so 'finished' never quietly means 'finished, with three cards abandoned'.

specialRules.name: cancel-only-while-active
specialRules.note: CANCEL (a human stops the batch) applies while drafting, running or held.

specialRules.name: terminals-are-frozen
specialRules.note: done, doneWithEscalations and halted are frozen: re-running is a new generation with its own selection, policy and journal, not a mutation of a settled one.

noOpRule: An action that does not apply in the current state is reject(reason) — an observable no-op with post == pre, never a throw and never a silent return.
